title: Hairpin lace shawl
subtitle: A triangular shawl built from joined hairpin lace strips in fingering weight.
excerpt: Three graduated hairpin lace strips, joined and shaped into a triangle, create a lightweight shawl with an open loopy texture. Worked in fingering weight on a 5 cm frame.
sourceNotes: Multi-strip hairpin lace shaping for shawls is a well-documented technique in 20th-century crochet pattern books. The graduated strip layout and joining sequence here are original to Homemade.

glossaryTerms.definition: A crochet technique where yarn is looped around a U-shaped metal frame while a central chain is worked with a hook, producing a strip of looped fabric on each side.
A hairpin lace strip that is longer or shorter than the adjacent strip, used to create a shaped outline such as a triangle when the strips are joined.
A crochet row that links the loops from two hairpin lace strips together, creating a seam between them.

crochet.gaugeText: 20 loops per 10 cm of strip length on a 5 cm wide frame in fingering weight.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Triangular shawl approximately 140 cm across the top edge x 65 cm deep at centre back, blocked.

content.text: . The longest strip forms the centre back; two shorter strips flank it. Joining them side by side and tapering the outer edges creates a triangle.
Centre strip: 260 loops per side (130 cm). Side strips: 180 loops per side (90 cm). Work each strip with double crochet through the central loops in the standard hairpin lace method.
Align one side strip with the top 90 cm of the centre strip. Work a
pairing one loop from each strip per double crochet. Repeat for the other side strip on the opposite edge of the centre strip. The lower 40 cm of the centre strip hangs free as the shawl point.

Work 1 round of double crochet around the entire outer edge, working 3 double crochets into each corner loop at the top two corners. Weave in all ends with your tapestry needle. Block flat, pinning the top edge straight and the point down to achieve the stated measurements.
